problem: Learning hierarchical representations from asymmetric and noisy hierarchical knowledge is difficult because standard embedding methods interfere between semantic meaning and structural relationships.
approach: Polaris uses polar hyperspherical embeddings where angular geometry encodes hierarchy and radius encodes semanticity, employing exponential maps to learn unit-norm representations with structure-guided retrieval.
contribution: Achieves up to ~19 points improvement in top-K retrieval and ~60% reduction in mean rank over baselines across taxonomy expansion tasks.

problem: Existing flow matching and diffusion models for trajectory prediction ignore temporal correlations and spatial symmetries in N-body systems, complicating generation and limiting performance.
approach: GP-EquiFlow integrates vector-valued Gaussian processes to construct SE(3)-equivariant prior distributions that respect both spatial symmetries and temporal dynamics in flow matching.
contribution: Delivers more accurate predictions on N-body and molecular dynamics with fewer sampling steps than baseline flow matching approaches.

problem: Modern vision models rely on pointwise activations and softmax for nonlinearity, but this dependency may be unnecessary and introduces computational overhead.
approach: PolyNeXt replaces activation functions and softmax with Hadamard products to create polynomial alternatives within MetaFormer-style vision backbones (MLPs, convolutions, attention).
contribution: Matches or exceeds activation-based counterparts on ImageNet classification and ADE20K segmentation at multiple scales with reduced computational cost.

problem: Current VLM spatial intelligence benchmarks contain invalid QA pairs due to point-cloud reconstruction artifacts and misaligned annotations with video evidence, and assume full-scene access unavailable in practice.
approach: ReVSI re-annotates 413 scenes across 5 datasets to fix object labels and geometry, regenerates QA pairs with human verification, and provides frame-budget variants to match actual model inputs.
contribution: Enables more reliable and diagnostic assessment of spatial intelligence, revealing systematic VLM failure modes obscured by prior benchmarks.

problem: Variable clustering in multi-factor block models lacks efficient and principled approaches that connect to robust optimization.
approach: Connects variable clustering to regularized subspace clustering through distributionally robust nodewise regression with convex relaxation and ADMM algorithm.
contribution: Demonstrates superior performance on clustering tasks through a principled, data-driven approach for robust region selection.

problem: Offline LLM-based recommendation using GFlowNets suffers from non-identifiability in Sub-Trajectory Balance due to partial support on the dataset-induced DAG, causing probability mass to allocate to unsupported regions.
approach: CFlower introduces a conservative SubTB objective that explicitly penalizes unsupported forward flow mass and combines dataset-constrained policy learning with on-policy sampling on the dataset DAG.
contribution: Improves distributional matching and delivers stronger accuracy-exposure trade-off than GFlowNet and SFT baselines on Amazon recommendation datasets.

problem: Chain-of-thought reasoning in LLMs carries substantial latency and compute costs, but the fundamental question of how many reasoning tokens are necessary as input size grows remains unanswered.
approach: Extends the bounded attention prefix oracle (BAPO) model to prove lower bounds on CoT tokens for binary majority, triplet matching, and graph reachability, showing Omega(n) scaling.
contribution: Identifies fundamental bottlenecks in inference-time compute through CoT, with empirical validation on frontier models showing linear reasoning token scaling.

problem: Monitoring treatment effects in online experiments with delayed outcomes and staggered entry requires robust methods that handle asynchronous potential outcome times and environmental nonstationarity.
approach: Adopts design-based perspective with carefully chosen arm-specific event-time filtrations to construct confidence sequences for treatment effects using arm-level IPW estimation.
contribution: Enables anytime-valid inference for delayed outcomes while outperforming traditional design-based variance bounds.

problem: Existing panoramic image editing methods fail to preserve global consistency because they ignore spherical geometry and use perspective-based approaches or cube-map decompositions.
approach: World-Shaper reformulates editing directly in equirectangular projection with distortion-aware attention modulation, layered shape loss, and curriculum training to internalize panoramic priors.
contribution: Achieves superior geometric consistency and editing fidelity on a new PEBench benchmark compared to state-of-the-art methods.

problem: Probabilistic forecasting with exogenous variables faces topological disparity in sampling initialization and spurious covariate correlations during iterative generation, limiting robustness.
approach: KITE introduces a History-Conditional Manifold for informative sampling initialization and a Knowledge-Guided Conditioning module using statistical priors to regularize variable interactions.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both deterministic and probabilistic forecasting with exogenous variables.

problem: Distributionally robust assortment optimization under the contextual MNL model requires algorithms that handle worst-case distributional deviations across multiple divergence measures.
approach: Leverages strong duality from distributionally robust optimization integrated into assortment procedures to develop polynomial-time algorithms for TV, KL, and chi-square divergences.
contribution: Provides theoretical analysis and establishes sample complexity bounds for all three robust MNL formulations.

problem: Video LLMs struggle with complex events requiring integrated spatial and temporal reasoning, and existing methods handle either dimension in isolation.
approach: VideoLoom uses a curated character-centric dataset with temporally grounded and spatially localized captions to train a unified Video LLM for joint spatial-temporal understanding.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on spatial and temporal benchmarks with a novel metric for comprehensive evaluation.

problem: Language models are sensitive to single-token changes at high-uncertainty points, but the geometric basis of this sensitivity remains unclear.
approach: Derives an so(n)-valued 1-form depending only on token embedding geometry and shows its curvature is semantically meaningful through chess reasoning task analysis.
contribution: Demonstrates that token space geometry directly reflects internal problem representations, with transformations clustering by board region and piece importance.

problem: Gaussian Belief Propagation approximations lack theoretical guarantees for complex, loopy, non-Gaussian factor graphs despite being widely used in practice.
approach: Leverages Central Limit Theorem to prove that variable beliefs under BP converge to Gaussian distributions in sparsely-connected factor graphs obeying key assumptions.
contribution: Provides mathematical guarantee for when Gaussian approximations are valid, confirmed experimentally on stereo depth estimation.

problem: Tracking text in videos faces severe geometric distortions from perspective shifts, visual ambiguity across instances, and sensitivity to structural details—problems not addressed by general object trackers.
approach: SymTrack proposes a detection-free framework with Cross-Expert Calibration to reduce bias and Predictive Token Rectification to correct structural imbalances.
contribution: Sets state-of-the-art on three benchmarks with up to 11.97% AUC improvement, enabling practical video text manipulation.

problem: Evaluating music-dance co-generation requires measuring rhythmic coupling at fine temporal resolution, a dimension not captured by generic audiovisual metrics.
approach: TMD-Bench integrates computable physical metrics with perceptual judgments via a rhythm-aligned dataset and fine-grained Music Captioner for structured semantics.
contribution: Reveals that commercial audio-visual models produce high-quality outputs but leave rhythmic coupling suboptimal, establishing evaluation standard for music-dance generation.

problem: Learning reward functions from human preference feedback requires accuracy across the entire state-action space for safety and transferability, not just on visited states.
approach: Derives minimum interaction requirements for compatible reward identification under deterministic preferences and formalizes connections to the Bradley-Terry model for stochastic preferences.
contribution: Establishes theoretical foundations for online compatible reward identification with characterization of problem complexity and sample efficiency.

problem: On-robot deployment of VLA models is bottlenecked by real-time inference under tight cost and energy constraints across heterogeneous edge accelerators.
approach: Provides systematic co-characterization via Cost-Energy-Time (CET) leaderboard and uncovers two-phase inference pattern (compute-bound VLM, memory-bound Action Expert), proposing DP-Cache and V-AEFusion for acceleration.
contribution: Achieves up to 2.9x speedup on GPUs and 6x on edge NPUs with only marginal degradation, showing edge devices can be more efficient than flagship GPUs.

problem: Existing multi-concept unlearning methods fail to remove multiple concepts from diffusion models without significant quality degradation or high hyperparameter sensitivity.
approach: FIA leverages model sparsity to identify Concept Sensitive Neurons via Contrastive Concept Saliency and Concept Agnostic Neurons, creating unified multi-concept masks.
contribution: Achieves more reliable multi-concept unlearning while maintaining generation fidelity with training-free, plug-and-play application.

problem: Diffusion LLMs face accuracy-parallelism trade-off where aggressive parallel decoding (high TPF) degrades task accuracy, limiting practical deployment.
approach: LightningRL uses Group Relative Policy Optimization with per-reward decoupling, NLL regularization, and dynamic TPF-aware filtering to optimize for both accuracy and parallelism.
contribution: Advances Pareto frontier across math and code tasks with average TPF of 7.3 while maintaining competitive accuracy.

problem: Optimal experimental design for MNL bandits is computationally intractable due to the combinatorial action space, lacking efficient algorithms with statistical guarantees.
approach: Proposes computationally efficient framework via 0-1 MILP reformulation with solver-certified stopping and fully polynomial-time lifted design using tractable surrogate objectives.
contribution: Establishes near G-optimality guarantees and instance-dependent sample complexity of O(d log N / Delta^2) for best assortment identification.

problem: Preference alignment for LLMs requires costly high-quality positive examples and intensive computation, motivating more efficient alternatives.
approach: U2A links preference alignment with LLM unlearning via bi-level optimization to quantify effects of negative example unlearning and select examples optimally.
contribution: Demonstrates cost-efficient preference alignment through selective unlearning of negative examples.

problem: Detecting AI-generated images is insufficient without addressing visible artifacts and restoration, leaving a disconnect between detection and practical correction.
approach: GenShield proposes unified autoregressive framework with Visual Chain-of-Thought curriculum learning for explainable AIGI detection and controllable artifact correction.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on AIGI detection benchmarks while enabling high-quality artifact correction with explicit stopping criteria.

problem: Nonparametric IV regression using spectral features fails when the true causal function is poorly represented by dominant singular components.
approach: Augmented Spectral Feature Learning makes feature learning outcome-aware via contrastive loss from an augmented operator incorporating outcome information.
contribution: Maintains effectiveness under spectral misalignment through task-specific feature learning.

problem: PINNs training is paralyzed by gradient pathology where PDE residuals and boundary constraints generate opposing gradients that trap the model in local minima.
approach: CAML reformulates zeroth-order terms into aligned constraints and introduces delay factors to help the optimizer skip high-curvature regions.
contribution: Significantly enhances numerical stability and efficiency in complex PINN problems.

problem: Standard zeroth-order gradient estimators suffer from O(r^2) truncation bias at smoothing radius r and bias-reduction schemes typically increase variance.
approach: Romberg-ZOGE forms Romberg-extrapolated linear combinations at radii {r/2^k} with reused perturbation direction, achieving O(r^{2R+2}) bias while preserving leading variance.
contribution: Demonstrates faster and more stable zeroth-order SGD on synthetic benchmarks, simulator-based wireless optimization, and black-box prompt tuning.

problem: Rubric-based LLM evaluation benchmarks lack systematic robustness validation, potentially tolerating significant semantic failures and irrelevant content additions.
approach: RubricRobustness applies systematic sensitivity analysis with semantic negation, stochastic deletion, and irrelevant addition perturbations to HealthBench and WildBench.
contribution: Reveals systematic vulnerabilities in popular benchmarks and establishes perturbation-based sensitivity analysis as prerequisite for evaluation validity.

problem: MLLMs in stateless systems are vulnerable to semantic-aware attacks where a single perturbation hijacks multiple decisions without model-specific tuning.
approach: SAUP acts as semantic router using theoretical analysis of latent space geometry to guide SORT optimization and annotates fine-grained semantic dataset.
contribution: Achieves 66% attack success rate on five targets using single frame against Qwen, exposing fundamental feasibility of semantic-aware hijacking.

problem: Ultra-high-resolution video generation requires handling compounded motion modeling, semantic planning, and detail synthesis simultaneously with prohibitive memory and computation.
approach: LUVE employs three-stage architecture: low-resolution motion generation, latent-space upsampling, and high-resolution refinement with dual frequency experts.
contribution: Achieves superior photorealism and content fidelity in UHR video generation.

problem: Unbalanced incomplete multi-view clustering is hindered by observation bias where missing patterns vary across views, causing learned associations to fail on incomplete samples.
approach: CIMLN uses context-aware meta-generation for view recovery and causal-invariant structure learning via counterfactual masking to enforce consistency across observation patterns.
contribution: Effectively alleviates observation bias for unbalanced incomplete multi-view clustering.

problem: Long-sequence modeling faces fundamental trade-off between fixed-size compressive memory (RNN efficiency) and lossless growing memory (Transformer fidelity).
approach: Artificial Hippocampus Networks maintain sliding KV cache as short-term memory while learnable AHN recurrently compresses out-of-window information into fixed compact long-term memory.
contribution: Outperforms sliding window and full-attention models with 40.5% inference FLOP reduction and 74% memory cache reduction on LV-Eval and InfiniteBench.

problem: Skill-based agent systems introduce unexamined security attack surface where backdoors can be embedded at skill level and propagated through skill composition.
approach: SkillTrojan embeds malicious logic in skill implementations, partitions encrypted payload across benign-looking invocations, and provides automated synthesis of backdoored skills.
contribution: Achieves 97.2% attack success rate while maintaining 89.3% clean accuracy on EHR SQL, exposing critical blind spot in skill-based agent architectures.

problem: Standard attention mechanisms treat scores as probability distributions, but dynamic MLP perspective reveals this may not be the optimal framing for autoregressive sequence modeling.
approach: HyperMLP/HyperGLU view attention heads as dynamic two-layer MLPs whose weights come from context history, using reverse-offset layout to align temporal mixing with autoregressive semantics.
contribution: Consistently outperforms softmax-attention baselines under matched parameter budgets.

problem: MoE architectures suffer from poor expert specialization where experts share overlapping spectral components and dominant gradient subspaces, limiting effective capacity.
approach: SD-MoE decomposes parameters and gradients in spectral space to separate dominant components and prevent gating from routing along shared directions.
contribution: Improves performance with effective expert specialization and minimal computation overhead, seamlessly integrating into Qwen and DeepSeek.

problem: Autonomous AI scientists bottlenecked by labor-intensive generation of publication-ready academic illustrations for research workflows.
approach: PaperBanana orchestrates specialized agents for reference retrieval, content/style planning, image rendering, and iterative refinement via self-critique using VLMs and image generation.
contribution: Outperforms baselines on PaperBananaBench (292 NeurIPS cases) in faithfulness, conciseness, readability, and aesthetics.

problem: Dropout scheduling is typically constant, but standard practice may suboptimally utilize dropout's regularization potential under fixed computational budget.
approach: Mean-field theory at edge of chaos shows dropout shifts perfect-alignment fixed point, enabling front-loaded schedules via critical scaling laws for smooth and kinked activations.
contribution: Front-loaded dropout schedules cut test loss by 18-35% over constant dropout in MLPs and Vision Transformers with no additional cost.

problem: Standard metrics like perplexity fail to guide mid-training toward SWE-bench performance due to long-context tax and weak downstream correlation.
approach: HE-SNR redefines intelligence via entropy-compression into low-order states and validates this metric on models up to 560B parameters across 32K/128K context windows.
contribution: Provides theoretical foundation and practical tools for optimizing LLM latent potential in complex engineering domains.

problem: Reconstructing RAW sensor data from RGB requires bridging information loss and complex ISP transformations—generative models are high-quality but slow; regression is fast but over-smooths.
approach: SHADE uses single-step deterministic flow with Homogeneous Representation Alignment via student-teacher DINO for alignment in shared feature space.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on multiple benchmarks with efficient and accurate sensor data reconstruction.

problem: Diffusion models designed for dense data waste computation on mostly-zero entries and erase sparsity patterns when applied to sparse continuous data.
approach: Sparsity-Exploiting Diffusion models only non-zero values, skipping zeros during training and inference while preserving sparsity.
contribution: Matches or surpasses conventional DMs and domain-specific baselines on physics and biology benchmarks with computational savings.

problem: Looping (layer reuse across depth) and depth growing (shallow-to-deep training) both improve reasoning but their relationship is unclear.
approach: Provides mechanistic unification showing looped and depth-grown models exhibit convergent depth-wise signatures with increased late-layer reliance and recurring patterns.
contribution: Shows inference-time looping on depth-grown models improves accuracy on reasoning primitives by up to 2x despite no loop training.
